office_does: State Representatives write and vote on state laws and the state budgets; this seat is one of two House seats for District 28 in Pierce County.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Mari Leavitt, in the House since 2019, faces Republican Kathy Richardson, a 20-year Army officer and nurse practitioner who has not held public office. Both lead with military ties; they differ most on state spending.

candidates.summary: House member since 2019 and Deputy Majority Whip, a former community college administrator and Pierce County human services deputy director who runs on a bipartisan record.
highlights: Voted for ESSB 6346 and the 2025 B&O tax bill, against the 2025 capital gains, services sales tax and gas tax bills [S6][S12][S14][S16][S20]
Says she "worked with law enforcement to secure resources and tools" [S1]
Endorsed by labor, police and sheriffs' groups, the Association of Washington Business and Planned Parenthood [S4][S24][S25]

taxes.basis: Split record: yes on ESSB 6346 and ESHB 2081; no on ESSB 5813, 5814 and 5801.

spending.basis: Cites investment in childcare, training, K-12 and affordable housing; sits on Appropriations.

housing.basis: Backs emergency and affordable housing investment but voted against the 2025 rent-increase limit.

safety.basis: Says she secured resources and tools for law enforcement; endorsed by police, sheriff and trooper associations.

experience.basis: In the House since 2019, in caucus leadership and co-chair of a joint committee.

social.basis: Voted for ESSB 5599; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and ProChoice Washington.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list and for ESSB 5599; no statements on the topic.

candidates.summary: Army veteran of 20 years, nurse practitioner, former Pacific Lutheran University associate dean and small business owner, running on budget accountability and affordability.
highlights: Says government should "budget like families do" and cites State Auditor findings on accountability [S5]
Questions whether current spending levels are sustainable if high earners and businesses leave [S6]
Frames public safety as both "safety and order" and treatment, saying "we cannot arrest our way out of every problem" [S7]
Attributes housing costs partly to permitting and regulation and wants fewer "unnecessary barriers and delays" [S8]

spending.basis: Repeatedly calls for a government that 'lives within its means', budget discipline and audit accountability.

taxes.basis: Cites concern about 'additional taxes and fees' and warns that high-income taxpayers may leave; no explicit pledge on any tax.

housing.basis: Blames permitting costs and regulatory complexity in part and wants fewer barriers and delays, while also 'protecting neighborhoods.'

safety.basis: Pairs support for law enforcement and order with treatment, prevention and police accountability.

experience.basis: Has held no public office; background is military, health care, education and business.
